headline: DayOne Data Centers, a Singapore company that builds and runs data centres for AI customers, has filed to list its shares on the US Nasdaq exchange.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 6: a public IPO filing by a large AI data-centre company, confirmed by its SEC filing, with the price and size still unset.
importance_line: What changed is that a builder of AI data centres has moved from private funding to asking public investors for money, which matters to investors who may be offered shares, then to the data-centre industry, then to other operators planning listings, and the doubt is that the size and price are not set, losses are widening and, The Business Times reports, one unnamed customer supplied 69.2% of first-half revenue.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Straits Times, that DayOne Data Centers filed publicly with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 5 Oct 2026 to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol DODC, and that its filing shows revenue of $512 million for the first half of 2026, more than three times the year before, alongside a net loss of $81.9 million, up from $13.5 million. Bloomberg earlier reported that the company, which filed confidentially in August, could seek as much as $5 billion at a value of about $20 billion, and The Business Times adds that the prospectus says two existing customers have been designated “Chinese military companies” by the US Department of War.
notes: Bloomberg's page could not be opened (HTTP 403); the original's link is kept for credit. Bloomberg's text was read on The Straits Times (credit BLOOMBERG), with The Business Times and Renaissance Capital for the prospectus. Possible duplicate of C07-12 (Reuters, DayOne IPO filing). The filing is dated 5 Oct 2026 US time (The Business Times dates it 6 Oct, Singapore time). Renaissance Capital estimates a raise of about $3.0 billion; Bloomberg's earlier figure is up to $5 billion.
